# EXP-010 results (generated by `edgelab.analysis.exp010 analyse`; AUC x 100, paired bootstrap over videos, 1000 resamples)

YOLOv8s cost factor r = 2.507 (8s detector 79.81 ms vs 8n 31.83 ms); keep masks seed 1; G = 8.

Pre-registration: `plan.md` (frozen 2026-11-07 17:00). Rows: `~/thesis-data/exp010/rows.jsonl`, per-frame scores `~/thesis-data/exp010/scores/`,
verdicts `~/thesis-data/exp010/verdicts.json`, run log `log.md`. SKIP is `deadline_replay.run_cell` re-implemented step by step to also give the paper
variant (checked: identical live AUC, drop rate and segment count on SHT-L0-8n s = 3). No condition, group, speed, policy or rule was added.

## Step 0: cost factor of YOLOv8s-pose
VM `edge-os`, cell L3-E0-R640-c0.25-O0-B4 (12 videos x 40 frames, co-load on), static ONNX 384x640 (sha256 9fea9f3e...2d03, weights sha256 234314cd...cfb3,
parity with Ultralytics: max keypoint difference < 0.17 px). 3 repetitions, host load outside the VM 6.7 / 6.8 / 12.0% (limit 30%): none excluded.
Mean detector time (pre + infer + post): 8s 79.81 ms (1,440 frames); 8n 31.83 ms (5 usable EXP-004 runs, 2,400 frames). **r = 2.507.**
Sensitivity: 8n re-timed in the same window (3 runs, 6.9-11.9% outside the VM) gives 31.88 ms, r = 2.503. The 8s trace is the 8n trace with each frame's detector time multiplied by r.

## Threats and caveats (read before quoting the verdicts)
1. **C2 passes only through a degenerate cell.** SHT-L0-8s at s = 6 (keep rate 9%) has 30 scorable windows for FILL (34 for SKIP) in the whole test set and
   0.000 fill coverage; its "significant" +3.20 [+2.28, +4.10] is a difference between two nearly constant score series (paper variant: -0.39 [-1.53, +0.54]).
   Without that cell, C2 would be 3 of 6 groups at s = 6 (SHT-L0/L2/L3-8n) and fail. The rule as frozen counts it, so C2 passes, but the 8s s = 6 results do not carry evidence about prediction.
   UB-L0-8s at s = 6 (coverage 0.10) is the same regime. P fill with G = 8 cannot bridge gaps of ~10+ frames (8s at s = 6 processes ~1 frame in 11).
2. **UBnormal is weaker.** UB-L0-8n is not significant at either speed (+2.24 [-1.91, +6.03], +3.61 [-0.48, +7.77]); UB-L0-8s only at s = 3. C1's 5 significant groups are 4 ShanghaiTech + UB-L0-8s;
   C2's 4 are all ShanghaiTech. All 12 live FILL-HOLD - SKIP point estimates are positive (smallest +2.24).
3. **The score-holding rule matters but does not explain the whole effect.** FILL-NORMAL - SKIP is positive in 11 of 12 live cells (significant in 9; mean +2.94); FILL-HOLD - SKIP has mean +5.65.
   So roughly half of the FILL-HOLD gain comes from holding the last score on blank frames (FILL-HOLD - FILL-NORMAL ranges from -0.15 to +5.4 by cell) and the rest from filling itself.
   The earlier EXP-009 contrast was confounded by exactly this; C3 (+5.65 mean) is the hold-rule-matched number.
4. **Different time scales.** SKIP's 24-pose window spans 24 *processed* frames (60-90% of real time skipped), FILL's spans 24 real frames. That is part of the policy contrast, not a bug, but it means the comparison is "predict at real time" vs "re-index", not prediction alone.
5. **Coverage is not comparable across arms.** SKIP always delivers a (held) score (coverage 1.0 by construction); FILL coverage counts frames with an own scored window.
6. **One mask draw.** Keep masks use seed 1 only (one draw per video); the CIs resample videos, so they do not include variability of the mask draw. The 8s traces are scaled 8n traces (only the detector part x r; tracker/STG-NF times and their variance unchanged).
7. **No multiplicity correction** over 12 cells x 2 variants; the verdict rules are the frozen counting rules. Absolute AUCs are low (50-66): the gains sit on a weak base (the unfilled SHT-L0 offline AUC is 68.5 / 66.2).
8. **Latency.** P is causal (no delay); FILL-HOLD's held scores are stale by up to the length of the blank stretch.

## Lead review (2026-11-07 17:45)

- **All four pre-registered checks pass by their rules** (C1 5/6 at s 3; C2 4/6 at s 6; C3 mean +5.65; C4 both 8s
  groups positive at s 3). Under §3 the claim is formally allowed.
- **Degenerate cell disclosed:** SHT-L0-8s at s 6 drops 91% of frames; SKIP keeps 34 and FILL-HOLD 30 scorable windows
  in 107 videos; both arms are at chance (paper 50.5 vs 50.1; live 52.5 vs 55.7). Its "significant" live +3.20
  [+2.28, +4.10] reflects causal smoothing over almost no scores, not a rescue; the paper variant is −0.39 [−1.53,
  +0.54]. It counts toward C2 under the frozen rule (4/6); **without it C2 would be 3/6 (fail)**. The plan had no
  pre-registered rule for cells where both arms collapse — a lesson, not a reason to drop the cell post hoc.
  Both readings are reported.
- **Honest summary:** the rescue is confirmed robustly at s 3 (5/6 significant, +5.7 to +8.3 live, incl. both
  detectors and UBnormal-8s) and at s 6 for all three ShanghaiTech-8n groups (+6.1 to +7.4). It is **not**
  significant on UBnormal-8n at either speed (+2.2, +3.6; positive point estimates), and it **cannot rescue a device
  that drops > ~90% of frames** (8s at s 6: both policies collapse; UB-L0-8s s 6 +3.84 n.s. live).
- The scoring-rule confound flagged in EXP-009 did not create the effect: with the *same* hold-last rule for both
  arms (FILL-HOLD) the gain is larger than with EXP-009's rule (FILL-NORMAL).
- **On "the hold rule explains half the gain" (code lane's caveat):** SKIP itself holds the last score, so FILL-HOLD
  vs SKIP (+5.65 mean, live) is the like-for-like comparison and isolates filling. FILL-NORMAL (+2.94) differs from
  SKIP in two ways (fill + blank frames scored "normal"), so it understates the filling effect; it is reported for
  continuity with EXP-009 only.
- **Additional threat:** a single keep-mask draw (seed 1); CIs cover video sampling, not mask-sampling variability.
  A second seed would be the cheapest strengthening (~30 min).
